# Preface.

## Beloved Reader/

->I.<-

However unnecessary and insignificant the subject matter described here might seem in the eyes of reason, it has nonetheless always been important and venerable according to the judgment of the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: "H. Geistes"</note>, as He has dealt with it so minutely and extensively in the writings of the Apostles and Prophets. It is indeed well known enough what frivolous and shameful thoughts and words regarding <term>chastity<note>The term "Keuschheit" here refers to moral and sexual purity as defined by religious law.</note></term> and marriage are common among the children of this world <note>A phrase used to describe those who prioritize secular life and physical pleasures over spiritual duties.</note>—so much so that even the most holy expressions of the Spirit of **God** cannot remain unreviled by the impure spirit of this world. Experience also shows that at times an impure mindset regarding such important matters has even prevented well-meaning souls from contemplating and honoring them according to their pure and innocent foundation.

<summary>In this preface, the author defends the spiritual dignity of discussing marriage and purity, arguing that despite worldly mockery, these topics are treated with great reverence in the Holy Scriptures.</summary>
<keywords>preface, Holy Spirit, chastity, marriage, purity, biblical authority, children of the world</keywords>

# Preface.

Which may to some extent be the reason why one finds so little concerning the **state of marriage** in the writings of the <term>Mystics<note>original: "Mysticorum"; authors focused on the inner spiritual life and direct union with God, who often prioritized celibacy over domestic life.</note></term>, since marriage is generally regarded only as something external and minor—something that, according to the claims of the **Papist clergy**, belongs only to the laity and worldly people.

->II.<-

Nonetheless, it is also evident enough from the literal word of Scripture how the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: "H. Geist"</note> connects and links the highest mystery and the single most important purpose of all divine teaching—namely, the union of man with **God**—with true marriage. Indeed, this matter—namely the virginal and married state—extends and spreads through the entire <term>divine economy<note>original: "œconomie"; in this context, the historical plan and management of God's interactions with humanity throughout time.</note></term> and God's provision for the restoration of fallen man. From the very beginning at the first creation of **Adam**, his virginal state, united with the **wisdom of God**, appears; and finally, in his restoration, this very same Divine marriage and union will be, so to speak, the final act on the stage of all of **God's** works. This is not to mention how, even in an external sense, one of these two ways of life <note>Referring to either the state of celibacy/virginity or the state of marriage.</note> must affect each and every person in the world.

<summary>The author argues that despite the low view of marriage held by some mystics and the Catholic clergy, the Holy Spirit uses marriage as the primary metaphor for the soul's union with God. He traces this theme from the creation of Adam to the final restoration of humanity.</summary>
<keywords>marriage, Mystics, Papist clergy, Holy Spirit, divine union, Adam, divine economy, restoration of man</keywords>

->III.<-

Furthermore, the great importance and depth of this matter is also evident because human reason and **hypocrisy** are so entirely blind and unwise in this regard and lead one astray. For not only are the extensive disputes between major factions well known, which may not be settled or decided according to the secret divine foundation for a long time yet; but there also arise among those who clearly see the general decay all sorts of significant <term>disagreements<note>original: "dissensiones"</note></term> and contradictions regarding the **married and unmarried life**. From these, alongside other <term>troubles<note>original: "incommodis"</note></term>, there especially arise many heavy transgressions involving perverse judgments, false propositions, immature proposals, and even worse <term>application<note>original: "application"; the practical implementation of religious or social rules.</note></term> of them. From this it may be sufficiently obvious that such things must certainly belong to a higher <term>sphere<note>original: "sphæram"</note></term> and order than perhaps the realm of reason, hypocrisy, or mere outward circumstances, because all of these cannot reach the heights and depths of the **great mystery** that lies in true **virginity and marriage**.

# Preface.

[...ho]ly work is far too deeply founded and fortified through many internal and external oppositions for it to be interrupted by desire or fear—not to mention being entirely thwarted. The essence of faith cannot and must not ever permit or suffer heights, principalities, angels, powers, and spiritual forces to separate it from the love of God in **Christ Jesus**: How then should minor circumstances and things do so? He who has first truly experienced how utterly insignificant all external matters, ways of life, and duties are compared to the most necessary work of the <term>new creature</term> <note>original: *neue creatur*; a biblical concept from the New Testament (2 Corinthians 5:17) referring to a person who has been spiritually transformed and reborn through faith</note> or creation, will well understand the mind of wisdom in its testimonies and guidance. Such a person will not interpret any external change in or before himself as a falling away from the inner truth. 

But he who does not yet know such ways does best to lay his hand upon his mouth <note>A traditional expression meaning to remain silent or refrain from judgment when one lacks understanding</note> and let no creature hinder or mislead him in his course, in which he must follow and become like **Christ** alone. In this way, much blame and resentment would be left behind, and the peace of God would hold its reign in the heart—to which the reader is earnestly commended.

**Quedlinburg**, the 12th of
**November** 1701.

# Chapter I.
## On True and False Chastity in General.

->I.<-

<margin>Necessary protection and warning.</margin>
In this consideration of the **married** and **single** way of life, that general reminder is also absolutely necessary: namely, that one should earnestly seek a pure, **evangelical** <note>In this historical context, "evangelical" (*evangelisch*) refers to a focus on the "Good News" of the Gospel and spiritual grace, rather than strict, legalistic religious rules.</note> mind in the **Spirit of Christ**. This is so that the soul does not fall into legalistic bonds and compulsion instead of that dearly purchased spiritual freedom, or into the excesses and hastiness of nature, and similar disorder, shame, and impurity. For it is from this that most of the many verbal disputes among the various parties of Christendom have arisen regarding these subjects: that very few have found the **middle path** between both extremes <note>original: *extremis*. The author is warning against both total rejection of marriage and total indulgence in it.</note> in divine moderation and wisdom. Instead, according to human reason and nature, they have followed the outward letter without distinction, favoring either the single or the mar-

<margin>Abstinence: what it is.</margin>

(a) It consists not only in the purity of the flesh, but also in the care of the body, in life and customs, because one must abstain from all unseemly things.

(t) Regarding other circumstances and scruples <note>Scruples: in a religious context, these are excessive worries or obsessive doubts about whether one has committed a sin.</note> of conscience in this matter, much is to be found in the writings of the Casuists <term>Casuists: theologians who study specific cases of conscience to determine what is or is not a sin</term>. 23. I must, however, mention here at last one most necessary condition, which is carefully established by those experienced in these matters. Therefore, a chaste wife is better than a proud virgin. For the former serves her husband chastely and humbly, but of the latter it is said: *You will save a humble people, and humble the eyes of the proud.* <note>original: "Du wirst ein niedriges volck selig machen/ und die augen der stoltzen demüthigen"; a translation of Psalm 18:27.</note> [z]

For whatever soul wishes to be a true virgin of Christ can be united with Christ in no other way than through lowliness of heart. 12. From this, it is now easy to examine and decide upon that opinion and saying which the world commonly puts forward regarding all marriages without distinction: that they are made or decided in heaven, and thus ordained by **GOD**, but only carried out on earth. For if one intended to include under the name of marriage all the impurities, shames, and sins that carnal people commit under it—using it as a cloak for their evil nature—then such things can no more be attributed to the most holy being or will of **GOD** without blasphemy than any other injustice. However, if one looks at the permitting direction and providence of **GOD**—how He wisely brings forth something healing even from the worst things for the benefit of the creature, finally after long patience and chastisement—then certainly **GOD’S** holy and permitting will (or that will which adapts itself to the condition of the poor creature) is not to be entirely excluded even from common marriages. Therefore they confess: **It is indeed good for a man not to touch a woman / however, so that this means should remain available to those who, because of their weakness, require the remedy of the married state.** (m) With the attached reason: **For it is indeed better to take a wife in a lawful manner than to live with harlots, or even to defile the wives of others.** (n) <note>The author is citing early Christian views that prioritize the legal and moral structure of marriage over the chaos of "fornication" or adultery.</note> And therefore they concluded with Paul: **Marriage is good because it preserves a man in moderation and does not let him fall into fornication, wherein he would perish and be destroyed.** (o) <note>Referring to the Apostle Paul's teachings in the New Testament, specifically 1 Corinthians 7.</note> However, they very carefully added the aforementioned unavoidable condition: namely, that one must use such a wholesome means in holy reverence and obedience to God in a truly blameless way, because otherwise there would be no difference between fornication and an immoderate use of marriage. <margin>Marriage of believers with unbelievers forbidden</margin>

(u) In contrast, he cited many testimonies from the Scripture to prove that one should not join oneself with unbelievers: such as Tobit 4:12; 1st Book of Moses [Genesis] 24:3; Ezra 10; 1 Corinthians 7:39, 6:15, 18; 2 Corinthians 6:14; and 1 Chronicles 11:4. 20. ...ingly, she divorced herself from her dissolute husband for that reason, after she—following the admonition of her friends—had been patient and silent for long enough, so that even her husband could bring no charge against her before the authorities. [g]

<note>original: "Justinus Martyr Apologia I. p. 44." This refers to Justin Martyr's *First Apology*, written around 155 AD. Justin describes a Christian woman in Rome who tried to reform her profligate husband but eventually issued a "repudium" (divorce) because his vices were so extreme that remaining with him was seen as participating in his sins.</note>

21. In such cases of adultery and the like, the ancient teachers carefully excused Christian spouses and testified that they did not seek such a divorce out of weariness or impatience, nor out of a secret desire for someone else or for something new and foreign—as might sometimes happen under a pretense of virtue. (h)

<note>original: "Hieronymus de Fabiola Epist. XXX. ad Oceanum." St. Jerome, writing in the late 4th century, defended the Roman matron Fabiola. She had divorced an abusive, adulterous husband and remarried, which Jerome argued was justifiable under the "law of Christ" even if it challenged certain social norms.</note>

No less blameless were those recognized in this regard who were *in fact* <note>original: "de facto"</note> cast out by their un-Christian spouses themselves, as happened very often during the times of persecution. (i)

<note>original: "Tertullianus Apolog. Cap. III. Arnobius Lib. I. adv. Gentes. p. 56." Tertullian (c. 155–220 AD) and Arnobius (c. 300 AD) both wrote about the domestic strife caused by Christianity; often, a pagan husband would divorce a wife simply because she had become a Christian, even if her character had improved.</note>

Apart from and without these specific circumstances, it remained the constant teaching of the earliest teachers that no spouse should leave the other. This lasted until, eventually, the mind of Christ on this matter was darkened and perverted by the frequently introduced human ordinances <term>human ordinances: man-made ecclesiastical laws and traditions that grew more complex over the centuries</term>, as is sadly well known and common enough among all religious factions today.

## Chapter IX.

# Of Holy and Pure Marriage.

->I.<-

After this brief consideration of the impure and unequal types of the married state, the question now arises: is any holy, pure, and blameless way of marriage before God actually possible or to be found? Unbelief and spiritual pride might be quick enough to answer with a denial, especially when the following difficult and far-reaching conditions are considered. And it is certainly true that a daily dying <note>German: *absterben*. In Pietist and mystical theology, this refers to "mortification"—the process of dying to one's own selfish desires and will to live for God.</note> and a bloody struggle against sin are required for this, and not merely lip-service or empty imaginings, which might easily and pleasantly suit the "old man" <note>A reference to the "old self" or sinful nature described in the New Testament (e.g., Romans 6:6).</note>. It is also certain that such examples are likely quite unknown; even if, here and there, such a divine marriage were actually conducted, the best and holiest works of God are commonly hidden from the eyes of reason <term>Reason: *Vernunfft*; in this context, it refers to human logic that lacks spiritual enlightenment.</term> and hypocrisy, and thus remain safe and <margin>Which marriage is holy</margin> unviolated. However, all of this cannot in itself nullify the matter or make it simply impossible, since—

7. One also reads the following explanations regarding this, particularly concerning the great harm that follows from it:

> "Those married couples who wish to <term>abstain <note>original: *enthalten*; referring to the cessation of sexual relations within marriage for religious reasons.</note></term> must agree unanimously on the matter. If he is overcome by lust and yet obtains no power [over the spouse's body], he finally falls into <term>fornication <note>original: *hurerey*; here used in the broad sense of any sexual sin outside the marriage bed caused by the denial of marital rights.</note></term>."

(k) All of this might well be confirmed by sad experience during the decline of Christianity, when ill-informed and undisciplined people, out of false intentions or thoughtless presumption, sometimes rushed in blindly and vowed abstinence, thereby falling into many temptations, as we shall soon see. Therefore, one still finds various letters from sensible teachers in which they earnestly advised against and rebuked such thoughtless things. We wish to present only a few passages here as a sample, as they may serve to explain this subject matter.

Indeed, this [divine love] is instead maintained and strengthened among those in whom the **transfigured JESUS** <note>original: *verklärte JESUS*; referring to Christ in his resurrected, glorified state</note> truly takes shape, and the **new creature** <note>A biblical reference to 2 Corinthians 5:17, meaning a person spiritually reborn</note> hastens toward growth, through this holy, chaste communion and impulse; when the souls seek nothing but **Jesus** himself and his love in one another, and with their inward eye gaze and remain fixed alone upon his holy, **virginal image of pure humanity** <note>original: *jungfräuliches bild der reinen menschheit*; a concept in mystical theology where the believer focuses on the spiritual, pre-fall perfection of humanity as mirrored in Christ/Sophia</note> (as it is glorified through the eternal Godhead and revealed in the new body). All of this, after long conflict and an earnest breakthrough, can be better experienced than described with words: although it cannot be denied that such examples may perhaps not yet be manifest.

# Chapter XIII.
## On general and special love.

->§. 1.<-

Because this subject <note>original: *materie*. Here referring to the nature of love and human relationships.</note> relates in many respects to what has been discussed thus far, and the presentation of it can therefore provide great light for married life as well, it will be beneficial to append something here; though not as an exhaustive treatise.

<margin>Distinction of love</margin>
Love toward our fellow man or toward our neighbor is of three levels and types, according to the nature of the people with whom one has to do. For it either has all people collectively before it whom it should love, and thus it is called **general love**; or it has to do with the pious and the faithful, which kind one calls **brotherly love**; or it finally extends to one or more **special friends** in a higher degree, which might be called **special friendship-love**, or also, in regard to the state of marriage, **marital love**.

<margin>and its types</margin>
2. None of these types abolishes the others or hinders and obstructs them, provided they are of the right kind

<meta>catchword: and</meta>

<summary>This page introduces a new chapter defining the three degrees of love: general love for all humanity, brotherly love for fellow believers, and special love directed toward close friends or a spouse.</summary>

Types of false love

2. That there is certainly a false love, and that not everything is true divine love which carries a pleasant name, appearance, and pretext of love, is seen quite clearly from the Scriptures. It names one type of love as hypocritical or feigned (Romans 12:9; 2 Corinthians 6:6; 1 Peter 1:22) when the false will—under outward appearance, caresses, good words, handshakes, and other flatteries—seeks only itself. There, the serpent <note>a reference to the tempter in Eden</note> slithers in even amidst the most intense, supposed devotions, sermons, and other spiritual exercises, through pleasant internal movements and mixed forces. These can certainly appear in the form of an angel <note>referring to the biblical warning that Satan disguises himself as an "angel of light"</note> and can enchant the person, if the Holy Spirit is not sought for His light. For a person who is just beginning to taste even a little of the heavenly gifts will, out of a lack of understanding, greedily grasp at all the forces, feelings, and pleasures that come before their mind. And when nature <note>human, carnal nature</note> mixes itself into the beginnings of grace, and "mixed love" mingles with the first sparks of divine love, the person easily accepts it all as pure and good; they rejoice for a while in a "strange light" and bathe, as it were, in such supposed waters of refreshment, believing they have found something truly righteous.

# Brief Preface by the *Author* <note>original: "autoris," the Latin genitive form of "author."</note> of these Observations.

What is shared here with the Christian reader, at the suggestion of a valued friend under this *title* <note>original: "titul."</note>, is released for printing with no other purpose than to provide those still unlearned in this *subject* <note>original: "materie."</note> more to reflect upon, and to provide the learned an opportunity for examination. This is done all the more willingly because the disputes regarding the married and unmarried life—the likes of which arose in Christendom long ago (stemming from opinions held by the *Encratites*, *Tatianists*, *Hieracites*, *Origenists*, *Abelonites*, *Sethians*, *Priscillianists*, and others <note>These names refer to various early Christian ascetic groups from the 2nd to 4th centuries who were often labeled heretical for their extreme rejection of marriage, meat, or wine.</note>)—have appeared once again in our own time. Even among pious people—some of whom argue too forcefully for the married life, while others favor the unmarried state—these disagreements have caused much discord until now.

<summary>In this preface, the author explains that the following text is intended to calm contemporary theological disputes over the merits of marriage versus celibacy by comparing them to ancient church controversies.</summary>

# Worthy of Consideration
## Observations
### On the Nature and Quality of the Married and Unmarried Life.

1. Man is created in the image of **GOD**.
2. **GOD** is a consuming fire. Also: **GOD** is a light / and dwells in a light / to which no one can come. According to the former property He is called a strong, zealous **GOD**. But according to the latter He is called merciful / gracious / and of great goodness; or / as John says / love.
3. According to both properties / (as these are considered in **GOD** without separation or conflict in the temperament <note>The term "temperatur" refers to a harmonious balance or "right mixing" of disparate qualities—here, the balance between God’s wrathful fire and His merciful light.</note> and sweet unity /) man was to be **GOD’S** image : just as it then also actually manifested itself in him in this regard / when he was created by **GOD** in righteousness and holiness according to both male and female properties.
4. The masculine is fire and wrath : The feminine is light and love.

<note>Note: Clement of Alexandria himself acknowledges this in Book III of his *Miscellanies* <note>original: "Stromat."</note>; regarding which see Annotation 67 below. <note>original: "Nota. Hoc ipse agnoscit Clemens Alexandrinus Lib. III. Stromat. de quo vide infra Annotat. 67."</note></note>

<summary>The author begins his treatise by defining the "image of God" in humanity as a balance of two divine properties: the masculine (associated with fire and wrath) and the feminine (associated with light and love).</summary>

5. Just as both properties are united and undivided in **GOD** as in one *substance* and essence: so too were they intended to be and remain united and undivided in man as in one *substance* and essence.

6. Therefore, Holy Scripture expressly testifies that man was initially created not in two, but in one *subject* <note>original: "subjecto"; here meaning a single individual entity</note> or *person*.

7. Indeed, the feminine was first united with the masculine in that same one *subject* or *person*: because the woman was subsequently taken out of and from the man during the separation of the two properties. *Genesis 2:21-24.*

8. Therefore, the passage <note>original: "Locus"</note> in *Genesis 1:27*—"And He (**GOD**) created them (mankind) male and female"—(provided that this refers to the manner and way of the very first creation, which this same verse clearly speaks of in the immediately preceding words, as does the seventh verse in the second chapter <note>This refers to Genesis 2:7, describing the formation of man from the dust</note>), is to be understood not so much as a male and female *person* in two different *subjects*, but rather as a male and female *essence* and property in one *person* and *subject*: otherwise, it would be difficult to reconcile <note>original: "conciliiren"</note> with the previously cited passage <note>original: "loco"</note> from *Genesis 2:18, 20-24.*

5. 7. It is "not good that man should be alone," *Genesis 2:18.* This occurred *out of an accidental cause* <note>original Latin: "ex causa adventitia"; a philosophical term meaning a cause that is not part of the original essence but arises due to external or subsequent circumstances.</note>, or from a newly arising cause. And it is remarkable that **GOD** spoke of this state precisely at the time when He—shortly before, to the man who was still alone (in the *singular number* <note>original Latin: "singulari numero"</note>) in verses 16 and 17—had presented the prohibition regarding the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

12. For **GOD** well recognized how the potential *center* <note>original Latin: "centrum"</note> of sin and deviation, following its hidden craving, was already stirring within the human will. And since **GOD**, out of special mercy, did not want to let man fall as deeply as the devil—which would have occurred if the awakened, fierce fire <note>In this mystical framework, "fire" represents the harsh, driving, or wrathful aspect of the soul that requires the balancing "light" of love to remain holy.</note> had completely swallowed the property of light and love within man—**GOD** separated the properties into two kinds of persons or *subjects* <note>original Latin: "subjecta"</note>. This was done so that, at the same time, from the divided feminine property of love, the designated and promised *Note Well* <note>original: "NB." (nota bene)</note> seed of the woman might be born as the true crusher of the serpent <note>original German: "schlangen-treter"; a reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the offspring of the woman would crush the head of the serpent.</note>.

**30.** However, in light of this, an important and difficult question arises, which has been debated time and again throughout Christendom: namely, whether and to what extent the outward state of marriage can coexist with Christianity, or not?

**31.** It is certain that Paul, in 1 Corinthians 7:1 and following <note>original: *seqq.*; an abbreviation for the Latin *sequentia*, meaning "and following."</note>, prefers the single state over the married state—provided that virginity occurs not only in the body but, first and foremost, in the spirit. Without this condition, outward virginity holds no advantage; instead, it is to be considered inferior to a modest marriage conducted in a fitting manner.

**32.** It is also certain that Christ himself especially praises those who, though they would otherwise be capable of married life, nevertheless make themselves eunuchs <note>original: *sich selbst verschneiden*; a reference to Matthew 19:12, where this is used metaphorically for choosing a life of celibacy for spiritual reasons.</note> for the sake of the kingdom of heaven and deny themselves the pleasures of such a life. See Matthew 19:10–12.

**33.** Now the question arises: is this then a general calling and counsel toward perfection <term>counsel toward perfection</term> <note>Historically, "counsels of perfection" were spiritual guidelines (like voluntary poverty or celibacy) considered helpful for spiritual growth but not strictly commanded for all believers.</note> that all Christians are bound to strive for? Is it such that no one can be a true and fully upright Christian if they do not comply with it?

If you have found her, then by all means let these three nights—as self-will, unchastity, and lusts of the flesh, over which the devil has power—pass by, so that you may remain alive and beget faithful children who are fit for the **kingdom of God**.

<header>### Concerning Marriage.</header>
<sig>Cc 5</sig>

Therefore, marriage is no small matter, to be undertaken so lightly with an earthly spirit or lust of the flesh, as the children of this world proceed with it. They think that if they can only satisfy their desire and then have a ceremonial service performed over it, they have then properly completed the marriage. But they do not pay attention to the punishments of sinners, which they prepare for themselves against the righteous judgment of the **Lord**. For in everything that a person chooses or accepts out of the covetous lusts of the flesh, therein they prepare for themselves a righteous punishment. If he sins in the body, he will be punished in the body; if he sins in the conscience, **God** punishes him therein. Every limb is punished in or with that in which it has sinned <note>This reflects the "talionic" principle that the nature of a sin determines the nature of its spiritual or physical consequence.</note>.

Now, however, one can clearly see that the vast majority—who undertake marriage for the sake of lust or the covetousness of the flesh under ceremonies alone—nevertheless live without the true marriage; that is, outside of **God's** sole essence <term>essence; original: "wesen"; refers to the divine substance or being that sustains spiritual life</term>, in which the godly life consists. Whereby the devil then has power over them, to bring them into all misery and unrest, and yet they think that they are married people: so that it is [as a certain writer has testified] nothing but an honorable harlotry <note>original: "ehrliche hurerey"; a common radical Pietist critique of marriages that are legally and religiously valid but lack spiritual "oneness" in God</note> before this desolate world.

# The Fourth Epistle.
## Concerning the mystery of holy marriage and the love of God.

The union of two into one must be kept holy and set apart. For when God grants such a union, it is He Himself who also preserves Himself in His virginal purity <note>In the mystical tradition of writers like Jacob Boehme, "virginal purity" refers to the "Heavenly Sophia" or Divine Wisdom, which is the spiritual counterpart to the soul.</note>. But no word is sufficient to express this treasure, and no human understanding is enough to grasp it.

He who possesses this treasure does not judge himself back into old ways; instead, he must judge and conform himself to this eternal, pure, chaste Spirit of Wisdom, just as it is unstained <term>unstained; original: "unbefleckt"; a theological term often used to describe Mary or the Soul as free from the "stain" of original sin or worldly lust.</term> and remains so. But if something else should be mixed with it, Wisdom flees from it and does not allow herself to be treated as something common, because she is not to be looked upon like those who turn from one person to another, or those of whom ten cling to one man <note>likely a reference to Isaiah 4:1, used here to criticize polygamy or spiritual infidelity</note>, even though a semblance of wisdom might be found among such people.

Thus, there was also only a semblance of wisdom among the ancients in their multiplicity <note>referring to the polygamy of the Old Testament Patriarchs</note>. But if someone today wished to make themselves like those holy women in multiplicity, he would lose the Child Jesus, for whose sake they did it <note>The author argues that the Patriarchs took multiple wives only to ensure the eventual birth of the Messiah; now that Christ has come, the practice has no spiritual purpose.</note>. # The VII. Epistle.
## Regarding the subtle snares of carnal love.

Sinful nature is always opposed to the pure spirit in all human beings / and all are born from the same root / only that it manifests and appears differently in one person than in another / this is true for evil / as well as for the gift of good in its manifold wisdom. The more subtle and seemingly righteous the sinful nature becomes / the more cunningly and hypocritically the serpent <note>A reference to the Devil or the tempter in the Garden of Eden, symbolizing internal deception.</note> can conduct itself therein / and the man of sin and of corruption can place himself all the more holily in Christ's stead / presenting himself as if he were God and inherently good. Therefore, such pleasure-seekers can teach nothing upright; rather, even if it has an appearance of truth, it only gives birth to confusion, disputation, and purely evil things. Indeed, even if they **awaken souls** <term>awaken souls: a term used in Pietist circles to describe the moment a person is first moved to religious concern or conviction</term> here and there with their disordered love, they still have no foundation or subsequent instruction to show such awakened souls how they should grow and work toward the **new birth** <term>new birth: a complete internal spiritual transformation or regeneration</term>.

For such souls are, in a certain way, only such **spiritual children** who are, as it were, conceived from an illegitimate bed. That is: they are not converted or even convinced in the purest, singular **love of God**, which remains a virgin and yet a constant mother in holiness to God, and which does not allow itself to be mixed with sinful flesh or tolerate [selfish] intentions for this or that.

Therefore, experience now teaches how a babbler, who sets himself up as a teacher, always awakens and produces more babblers; or at best, devises and imposes a **Pharisaic hypocrisy** <note>A reference to the biblical Pharisees, implying a focus on outward religious form and legalism while the heart remains unchanged</note>, or else gathers a society that is pleasing to the flesh, which does not even recognize the lusts within itself, much less dies to them <note>The concept of "dying to the self" or "mortification" is central to this mystical theology</note>. Because of this, they always fall into something else when they grow tired of one thing, and then seek to delight themselves here and there in order to satisfy their own [lower] nature.

Therefore, people use **God’s** word and call it "edification," <note>German: *erbauen*. A central term in Pietism referring to the building up of the internal spiritual life through prayer and study.</note> and [say] one should not neglect the assemblies, and so forth—where yet the speech of **God**, like silver and gold refined seven times, <note>A reference to Psalm 12:6: "The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times."</note> must be purified in the soul and proven in the person through the fire of tribulation. This speech of **God** remains well hidden under mixed teaching; for such teaching gives birth only to strife, disputation, and contradiction, even when using the most plausible and inherently good propositions.

On the other hand, it is our sole duty that we become heartily obedient to the living word of truth, and now also grow in the head **Christ**, and properly adorn the doctrine with one's life, and one's life with the doctrine, <note>This reflects the Pietist ideal that outward behavior and internal faith must perfectly mirror each other.</note> and be healthy in faith.

Now, whoever has perhaps fallen into the judgment of the slanderer <note>Likely referring to the "accuser of the brethren" (Satan) or to earthly critics who find fault with the believer's conduct.</note> in certain matters without this [foundation] does well if he refrains from all words and works by which others could be delayed in their misery or offended. But in particular, our duty remains to become strong in our most holy head in holiness and righteousness—to grow and to walk as **Christ** walked. Thus, the adversary may find nothing to blaspheme, and the accuser in the conscience before **God** may find nothing to accuse, but rather be cast out.

# The 15th Epistle.
## Concerning flattering, ungodly union.

->Greetings to the Reader<- <note>original: "L. S.," an abbreviation for the Latin *Lectori Salutem*, a standard greeting in formal letters of this period.</note>

What could possibly condemn a person if they make room for the power of the Son of **God** within themselves and sweep out all the desires and deceits of their own heart? For this is and remains true: that he who does not recognize **Jesus**, nor believes in him, has no eternal life. But whoever boasts that they know **God** must nevertheless constantly allow themselves to be judged and condemned, both inwardly and outwardly: Let that person see to it that their fear of **God** is not hypocrisy.

For where **Christ** is in truth, no true condemnation has a place. But the fact that a person is drawn back into a hell of anxiety comes from this: when they allow themselves to be taken captive by some desire. For this must afterwards always be condemned by the spirit.

However, whoever remains always in watching and praying <note>A central theme in Pietist spirituality, referring to the practice of constant self-examination and alert communication with God to avoid sin.</note> allows nothing to take them captive. For they love only **God**, and cling to Him, and let nothing into their heart that could poison or defile them, even if it should appear under a very good guise. <note>The author warns that even "good" things can become idols or distractions if they replace a singular focus on God.</note> Therefore Wisdom cries out: Guard your heart with all diligence! <note>A reference to Proverbs 4:23: "Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life."</note>

<keywords>internal purification, hypocrisy, spiritual vigilance, heart-guarding, condemnation, Pietist ethics</keywords>

There are, however, people who appear good-hearted, who cling to others and gladly steal spiritual strengths. In this way, some people cling so closely, hoping to obtain through this what might heal their souls. But they have no root together; instead, before they realize it, the lust of the flesh weaves itself in—almost as if in sleep—so that they fall into a dangerously lustful association.

But it is impossible to say how difficult it is to separate such souls from one another again. The more time they are given, the more shameless they become in this false love. Such lovers are, according to the judgment of the **Spirit**, "outside with the dogs," and can by no means enter into the city of **God**, even if they had already stood in paradise. <note>A reference to Revelation 22:15, "Outside are the dogs... and everyone who loves and practices falsehood." # The XVII. Missive.
## Regarding a sound judgment concerning the state of marriage.

The fact that **marriage** <note>original: *ehestand*, literally "the state of marriage."</note> is judged so inconsistently arises, among other reasons, because almost no one has enjoyed a **true marriage in God**; therefore, no true distinction can be made in any respect. And so most people tend to know and speak only piecemeal about **God** <note>original: *GOtt*.</note> himself, as well as about his ordinances.

Now, if someone has fallen into a **sinful state of marriage** and therein succumbed to a **vain plague of lust** <note>original: *eitele lust-seuche*. A very strong Pietist critique of marriages based purely on physical desire rather than spiritual union.</note>, they later seek to rectify it by rejecting marriage altogether. And so it goes with all other stations and offices.

However, if everyone first learned to rightly know their own **corrupt condition of the heart**, they would easily notice that they are just as confused in their own mind. And

# The XVIII. Missive.
## Concerning the gift of abstinence and the temptations therein.

The gift of **chastity** is a precious gift of **God** / and whoever has received it / is bound to take care / how he may please **God** / and cling to Him / so that he may become **one spirit with Him** <note>original: *ein geist mit ihm werde*. In a biblical sense, this refers to something "unclean" or "profane," as in Acts 10:15.</note>.

However, **God** forces no one into **abstinence** <term>Enthaltung: In this context, voluntary celibacy or refraining from marriage for spiritual reasons.</term> / just as little as He forces anyone into marriage. Rather, He leaves man to his free will / and wherever the will inclines in obedience / there He goes along. Meanwhile, it is certainly a delicate work concerning a chaste, holy soul / and **Christ** gladly dwells within her / and **betrothes Himself** to her: Nothing can bind her to a creature / but she is bound to **God** / and to nothing else.

Therefore, neither the devil / nor the world, nor the flesh has any right or claim on such souls

I wish and hope, my dear friend <note>Original: *m. l. ### Concerning certain duties of married couples toward one another.

Among married couples, it is a bad sign if one is always complaining or angry about the other, but never about themselves. # Of Marriage.

to be reckoned as a shame. For a thing, which in and of itself remains exactly the same, is made good or evil only through the goodness or wickedness of the heart. The sin that is committed in the **state of marriage** <term>state of marriage</term> <note>original: "ehestand" — refers to the spiritual and social condition of being married, rather than just the wedding ceremony</note> does not stem from the fact that marriage itself is evil; for it is nothing other than holy.

The Church is holy in itself: but the evil will of men has made it unholy and reprehensible before **God**; because they have changed the **divine institution** <term>divine institution</term> <note>original: "einsetzung GOttes" — refers to the original laws or ordinances established by God</note> within it. And the fact that one commits such great sins through the inclination toward this natural union stems from nowhere else but the wickedness of the heart; because the matter in itself is good and holy. 

Because man is so forgetful of God that he misuses all of God’s foundations and works, should he not therefore perish through his own wickedness? This is so even though he attributes all his faults to God himself; for if he were to fall into sin through **carnal lust** <term>carnal lust</term> <note>original: "fleischliche wollust" — physical desire or pleasure separated from spiritual intent</note>, he would say: "Why did God give me this natural inclination, through which I have sinned?" And if a **rod** <note>The "rod" (original: "ruthe") is a traditional metaphor for divine discipline or corrective punishment</note> were to chastise men, they would complain that God was tormenting them, or had even forsaken them. This is how they are accustomed to act in all things; and however great all their wickedness may be, nevertheless...

### XIII.

When shall I find You completely?

# XVII.
## Owed thank-offering of love. <note>original: "Schuldiges danckopffer." In a 17th-century Pietist context, a "thank-offering" is a poetic or musical expression of gratitude intended as a spiritual sacrifice.</note>

->To the tune: Praise / glory / honor / renown / thanks / power<-
->and might.<-

### 1.
Come, bow down low, my heart and mind,
->Before the Lamb’s throne in the dust below;<- <note>The "Lamb" refers to Jesus Christ, a central image in the Book of Revelation representing sacrifice and victory.</note>
Lay yourself down at his feet,
->And repeat your songs.<-
Recognize how you are nothing of yourself,
How God is everything in you and in all.

### 2.
Where would you have a spark of strength,
->If you did not receive it from above?<-
Who has obtained so much rest for you
->From your enemies' cunning and raging?<-
Who stilled the roaring of this sea,
And who conquered the power of hell’s army?

## XVIII.
# The New Creation through God’s Love.

**J**ehovah / <note>The Hebrew name for God, often used in this period to emphasize the eternal and covenant-keeping nature of the Divine.</note> take from me the powers
Wherein I am now held captive by you.
To you my heart and mind must be devoted /
Otherwise your Bride will not be fully pure for you. <note>The "Bride" is a metaphor for the individual soul or the Church in its intimate relationship with Christ.</note>

Let grow in the new creature <note>original: "creatur." Refers to the "new creation" in Christ described in 2 Corinthians 5:17.</note>
The pure mind toward a divine nature:
Which retains nothing of the old leaven, <note>original: "sauerteig." A biblical metaphor (1 Corinthians 5:7) for the lingering influence of sin or the old self that must be purged.</note>
And also makes a stony heart small and soft. <note>A reference to Ezekiel 36:26, where God promises to replace a "heart of stone" with a "heart of flesh."</note>

Therefore, gather all the power of love
To that which your hand now creates anew:
Because mind and heart and the course of thoughts
Offer themselves up to this work alone.

For does not the mind of an earthly Bride
Always focus on him to whom she has entrusted herself:
Should not my heart be always with its treasure,
Who leads me into the pure Godhead? <note>original: "Gottheit." Refers to the essential nature or being of God.</note>

### XVIII.

## The new creation through God’s love.

Jehovah, <note>A traditional transliteration of the Hebrew name for God (Yahweh), commonly used in 17th and 18th-century German hymns.</note> take from me the powers
By which I am now captured by You.
My heart and mind must be surrendered to You,
Otherwise Your Bride will not be entirely pure for You. <note>The "Bride" refers to the individual soul or the Church in a mystical marriage with Christ.</note>

Let grow in the new creature <note>original: "creatur." In this context, it refers to the "new man" or reborn soul described in 2 Corinthians 5:17.</note>
The pure sense for a divine nature:
Which keeps nothing of the old leaven, / <note>A biblical metaphor from 1 Corinthians 5:7, where "leaven" represents sin or the old, corrupt way of life.</note>
And also makes a stony heart small and soft. <note>An allusion to Ezekiel 36:26: "I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh."</note>

Therefore, gather all love’s power
To that which Your hand now creates anew:
Because mind and heart and the course of thoughts
Offer themselves up to this work alone.

Does not the mind of an earthly Bride
Go always to the one to whom she has entrusted herself?
Should not my heart always be with its treasure,
Who leads me into the pure Godhead?

The soul can never rest from thinking;
Her will always has something to do:
So shall it always of You, You highest Good,
Only eat, just as a strong hunger does.

O take deep root, you new life;
Let your growth never be hindered.
The new body draws God’s love into itself,
And drinks sweetly from Jesus’ breasts. <note>This "nursing" imagery was a common motif in 17th and 18th-century mystical devotion, symbolizing the soul’s total dependence and intimate nourishment from Christ.</note>

Thus the temple is built in secret,
A house of the mother for the Lamb’s bride, <note>In this context, the "mother" often represents the Holy Spirit or the "Heavenly Jerusalem," while the "Bride" is the individual soul or the Church.</note>
Where she lovely lures the bridegroom in,
To be kissed and known by Him.

Here she offers Him the new fruits,
And becomes aware of the hot love:
The more she gives, the more He gives Himself to her,
And directs her desires only inward.

Draw us after You, O strongest magnet,
Just as our love’s delight stands only toward You;
Hide the body of the new humanity in You,
So that this child remains safe from enemies. <note>The "magnet" is a favorite metaphor in Baroque and Pietist poetry for the irresistible pull of divine love acting upon the soul.</note>

Open Yourself, You name Jehovah,
In JESUS, who remains for us an eternal Yes! <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 1:20: "For all the promises of God in him are yea [Yes], and in him Amen."</note>
You open love, unconstrained faithfulness,
Make Your covenant in us ever new.

Create everything new in us, You speaking Word,
Keep open the gate of Jerusalem that was once burst open,
So that the redeemed number
May hold the Lamb’s meal within her walls. <note>The "Lamb's meal" refers to the Marriage Supper of the Lamb in the Book of Revelation, as well as the Eucharist.</note>

Does not the voice call out from Your temple:
O bride, keep your heart raised up to me!
Keep your garment along with heart and senses pure,
And hurry infinitely into my heart.

Yes, come, Lord Jesus, increase in us always,
And let us find rest in no other thing!
Draw us after You, so we run to You,
And follow as virgins forever and ever! <note>Refers to the "virgins" who follow the Lamb in Revelation 14:4, representing those who have remained faithful and pure in their devotion.</note>
